note: France with its overseas departments, territories and colonies, walked back from 2026.

reviewed.why: Metropolitan France with Corsica, the overseas departments (Guadeloupe, Martinique, French Guiana, Réunion, and Mayotte since 2011) and the overseas territories (Saint Pierre and Miquelon, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Martin, New Caledonia, French Polynesia, Wallis and Futuna, the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, Clipperton), whose borders have not moved since 1957
Algeria, Djibouti, the Comoros and Vanuatu, French (Vanuatu Anglo-French) until their independence, with today's borders

French West Africa, French Equatorial Africa, French Togoland, French Cameroon and Madagascar, with today's borders, from French rule to independence, and the British Southern Cameroons (Northwest and Southwest of today's Cameroon) until they join Cameroon in 1961

Morocco (without Western Sahara) and Tunisia: the French protectorates until 1956, with Spain's northern zone, the Tangier International Zone, Cape Juby (Spanish until 1958) and Ifni (Spanish until 1969)

French Indochina: Vietnam (Tonkin, Annam and Cochinchina, then the State of Vietnam), Laos and Cambodia, with today's borders, until independence in 1953 and 1954, then North and South Vietnam until 1976
French India: Pondichéry, Karikal, Mahé and Yanaon (today's Puducherry, with Mahé drawn where it is, not where Natural Earth puts it) and Chandernagore, until they pass to India

The Saar: a League of Nations territory from 1920 to 1935, German again until 1945, occupied by France, a protectorate of France from 1946 until it joins West Germany in 1957, with today's Saarland borders

Syria (with the Golan Heights), Lebanon and the Sanjak of Alexandretta (Hatay): French mandates under the League of Nations, with the states France set up in Syria (Aleppo, Damascus, the Alawites, Jabal Druze) until their union, with today's borders; Hatay State in 1938, Turkish from June 1939
Guangzhouwan, leased to France until 1945, then part of China
